taxonomic_note: True Croton capitatus is accepted, but historical Central Texas records under C. capitatus var. lindheimeri belong to accepted Croton lindheimeri. The learner card therefore remains concept-unresolved until true C. capitatus records are re-scouted under the modern split.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST — TRUE CROTON CAPITATUS (TAXON CONCEPT HOLD): a pale woolly annual resembling C. lindheimeri. Inspect FEMALE flower sepals at and after anthesis: about 7–10 mm (up to 15 mm in fruit), spreading widely with tips RECURVED OUTWARD, versus straight/slightly incurved sepal tips of C. lindheimeri. SOME true C. capitatus leaves may be blunt-tipped or mucronate, not nearly all acute. These are supporting traits, not a safe identification from pale hair alone. The two labeled NC State CC0 images illustrate actual woolly floral and leaf habit but DO NOT photographically prove the mature outward-recurved female sepal pattern. The old combination C. capitatus var. lindheimeri IS A SYNONYM of C. lindheimeri, not evidence for strict C. capitatus in Hays County. The taxon-concept and native-range HOLD remain untouched.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas state-level nativity is supported, but Central Texas records historically filed as C. capitatus var. lindheimeri are excluded because that concept now maps to C. lindheimeri. No three exact target-zone counties are assigned to strict C. capitatus.

best_field_traits: stems and leaves densely stellate-hairy with whitish to pale-yellow woolly pubescence
some leaf tips obtuse, rounded, or mucronate

persistent pistillate sepal tips spreading or recurving outward after anthesis
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The highest-value split from C. lindheimeri is sepal posture plus leaf-tip shape: true C. capitatus tends toward outward-flaring/recurved pistillate sepals and may show blunt or mucronate leaves.

comparisons.key_distinctions: The FNA split: strict C. capitatus has some obtuse/mucronate leaf tips, long persistent FEMALE sepals (about 7–10 mm, to 15 mm in fruit) that flare/recurve outward, and less strongly decreasing petiole lengths up the stem. C. lindheimeri is typically acutely tipped, ochraceous when young, with shorter (5–7 mm) straight/slightly incurved female sepals. Historical C. capitatus var. lindheimeri is C. lindheimeri. NC State exact-label photographs cannot prove true local Hays strict capitatus.

field_matrix.lindheimeri: Three styles each divided twice = often twelve tips
field_matrix.capitatus: Three styles divided 2–3 times = commonly 12–18 (sometimes more); not a consistent split

not_reliable_alone: White/light wool cannot alone distinguish C. capitatus from C. lindheimeri.
Male stamens do not prove pistillate sepal posture.
One blunt or one pointed leaf is insufficient: sample upper and mature leaves.
Old plant names using capitatus var. lindheimeri do not document strict capitatus.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.title: True capitatus — look for OUTWARD recurved female sepals, not just wool

steps.look: Stout hairy annual with small creamy male and female flowers
steps.what: Existing NC State photos illustrate this broad habit only, not confirmed local strict identity.

steps.look: Look for SOME blunt, rounded or mucronate leaf tips
steps.what: Supporting clue; mature leaves and position matter.

steps.look: Long 7–10 mm pistillate sepals flaring OUTWARD; may persist to 15 mm in fruit
steps.what: This is the key difference from C. lindheimeri; a paired stage-matched macro is needed.

steps.look: Petioles remain relatively similar length higher on stem
steps.what: Compare with the more marked decrease toward the tip in C. lindheimeri; secondary field character.

steps.look: Avoid 'capitatus var. lindheimeri' as evidence of true capitatus

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Strict Croton capitatus: unresolved local concept, use pistillate sepals
steps: Recognize woolly annual as a candidate, not a definite species.
Study multiple mature leaf tips: some may be blunt or mucronate.
Observe FEMALE flower sepals opening/flaring outward at anthesis, staying recurved in fruit.
Compare paired mature FEMALE sepals with C. lindheimeri (straight/slightly inward).
Do not attach older C. capitatus var. lindheimeri records to strict capitatus nativity.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Pistillate sepals OUTWARD recurved + some blunt leaf tips supports strict C. capitatus, if taxonomy independently verified.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: No installed images prove the key strict C. capitatus female sepal posture. Current target-zone concept remains unresolved and excluded from native certification.
